correctness.rationale: A bijective enumeration of the a+b cyclic phases gives exact first-order and second-order counts. The first scattered counter 01 has exactly gcd(a,b)-1 disjoint cross-family collisions. The independent formula for 001 has positive difference bm*s*(a-s)/2 on every such pair, proving injectivity of the joint signature. The minimal degree and exact gap follow. A four-run example is verified with all fourteen degree<=3 counts, and the truncated subsequence generating series proves persistence under powers. Standard-library checks independently recompute 9360 signatures and 30420 phase comparisons; these checks corroborate the proof but are not infinite certificates.

evidence: Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland, arXiv:2201.04603, introduce binomial complexity results for morphic and structured infinite words.
Vivion, arXiv:2509.11172, gives equality of binomial and factor complexities under particular balance and morphic hypotheses; these do not describe arbitrary long two-run periods.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem asserting degree-2 equivalence equals equality for balanced words cannot imply degree-3 rigidity for all two-run periods, many of which are not balanced. The general complexity statements in the inspected sources give no exact two-counter phase formulas or positive gap.

evidence: The degree-two gcd class count already appears in an existing related record; this new claim does not assert it as a separate original contribution.
The primary circular Parikh-matrix paper studies rotational averages rather than a sparse injective phase fingerprint.
The explicit primitive four-run conjugate pair demonstrates that universal degree-three rigidity across all binary cycles is false.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior second-order phase-class counts are a shared premise, not an implication of third-order injectivity: when gcd(a,b)>1, second-order collisions persist and require independent 001 separation. Averaged counts, generic binomial complexity and balanced-family equality results do not imply the joint sparse signature or the strict quantitative gap. The boundary example is included as a structural limitation and witness, not a broader universal claim.

evidence: Poovanandran–Simpson–Teh, arXiv:2110.14858, develop circular subword counts and averaged Parikh matrices. The average erases rotation phase; the theorem uses two phase-specific scattered counters.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The candidate concerns injectivity of the map from the cut position to the ordered pair of counts of 01 and 001. Rotational averaging does not supply a statement about this map. A circular average cannot recover its inputs. No inspected result states an equivalent phase-injectivity criterion.

evidence: The formulas in RESULT.md give a complete parametrization of precisely gcd(a,b)-1 degree-two phase collisions and a strictly positive 001 gap in each.
No exact tabulation of all one-zero-run/one-one-run cyclic phase pairs with the joint (01,001) signature was identified in the inspected primary sources.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The claim is a universally quantified phase-reconstruction and separation theorem rather than a finite table entry. Search absence does not prove novelty; the exact overlap with published tables, if any, remains a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The inspected closest sources on averaged circular Parikh matrices, general binomial complexities, and balanced-family degree-two separation do not imply a sparse two-counter, gcd-sensitive all-phase recovery theorem. Earlier degree-two gcd counts are explicitly credited and not treated as the new contribution. Comparison is limited by unindexed prior work.
residual_risks: A differently phrased or unindexed equivalent theorem on cyclic conjugates and scattered subsequence counts could exist.
No universal extension to arbitrary observation lengths or to cyclic words with more than two runs is asserted.

value.rationale: Cut-position recovery from a sparse scattered-subsequence deck is a natural combinatorial reconstruction problem. The result achieves phase injectivity with only two ordered-pattern counts, gives a sharp gcd-dependent minimal deck degree, exact positive integer separation gaps uniform in repeat count, and identifies a primitive four-run counterexample. The proof explains the structural arithmetic of collisions instead of only enumerating cases.
